title: Wire dispatch tokens into claim and lock as an optional, additive check
description: Design T-432, first worker task 2. No flag day: behavior is unchanged when no token is required.
acceptance_criteria: blackboard.py claim and lock.py acquire accept a token and verify it with token.py; a mismatch between token and the acting agent, task or role is refused.
Tokens are required only when the operator has signed a requirement for that epic; otherwise nothing changes. A test pins both cases.
The suite passes via goal_mode. Do not edit CLAUDE.md. Hand off to verifier.

notes.note: plan: wire dispatch_token.py into blackboard.py claim and lock.py acquire as optional additive gate; requirement lives inside the epic's own signed token set (required:true); claim consumes nonces single-use, lock acquire does not (refresh must keep working); waiting on T-456's lock on dispatch_token.py/test_dispatch_token.py to add epic_requires_token()+required field there

HANDOFF -> verifier: EXPECTED vs ACTUAL. Expected: an optional, additive dispatch-token check wired into
`blackboard.py claim` and `lock.py acquire`, zero behavior change when an epic carries
no operator-signed requirement. Actual: confirmed by goal_mode (full suite green, two
runs, ~110-120s each) and by a dedicated subprocess-driven test file
(.harness/tests/test_dispatch_token_wiring.py, 13/13 passing) plus a throwaway-tree
smoke script run by hand before touching the live files (built in scratch first, per
instructions).

DESIGN CHOICE (acceptance criterion 2). Requirement lives INSIDE the epic's own signed
dispatch-token set: dispatch_token.draft() gained a `required` bool, part of the signed
payload bytes (not a second, separately-signed record). New function
dispatch_token.epic_requires_token(root, epic) scans dispatch_tokens/DT-*.json for a
SIGNED, VERIFIED set naming that epic with required=true; unsigned drafts, wrong-epic
sets, and wrong-key signatures never count (pinned in test_dispatch_token.py's new
EpicRequirement class). No dispatch_tokens/ directory at all (today's live tree) means
epic_requires_token returns False with zero subprocess calls -- the "no flag day"
property.

NONCE DECISION (asked for explicitly). blackboard.py claim consumes nonces: single-use,
recorded into bb["used_dispatch_nonces"] inside the same guarded()/save_bb cycle that
performs the claim, so no second lock is needed. lock.py acquire does NOT consume
nonces: re-acquiring/refreshing a lock you already hold is the ordinary heartbeat
pattern and must keep working under the same still-valid token. Both choices are tested:
test_dispatch_token_wiring.py::RequirementIsEnforced::test_claim_nonce_is_single_use and
::test_lock_acquire_succeeds_and_refreshes_with_the_same_token.

NOT DONE / LEFT FOR THE OPERATOR OR A LATER TASK. No dispatch-token set has been
drafted or signed for any live epic -- this task only builds the mechanism and pins it;
whether any real epic's claims should actually require a token is an operator decision
(mint via `dispatch_token.py draft --epic <E> --dispatch <agent:task:role> --required`,
then sign with the printed ssh-keygen command). CLAUDE.md was not touched and needs no
documentation change for this task; the --token-file flags and the gate functions are
self-documented in each file's own docstrings/help text.

CAVEAT T-456 OVERLAP. dispatch_token.py and test_dispatch_token.py were held by
worker-g10-revoke for T-456 when I started; I worked on blackboard.py/lock.py first,
waited for the lock, re-read both files after acquiring, and layered my diff on top of

does NOT go through verify()'s revocation check (it has no agent_name to check a
revocation against) -- this is intentional (the requirement flag is epic-wide, not
agent-scoped) but a verifier should confirm that reading matches T-456's intent.

VERIFIED (verifier-g10-wire, different agent from worker-g10-wire). Replayed, did not trust the report.

Full suite: `python3 .harness/bin/goal_mode.py run --cmd "python3 -m pytest .harness/tests -q"` -> GOAL REACHED iteration 1/3 (111.24s), observed myself just now. `test_dispatch_token.py` 26/26, `test_dispatch_token_wiring.py` 13/13, re-run independently.

Own replay in a throwaway tree (copy of .harness/bin, own blackboard.json/tasks fixtures, own ssh-keygen root, not the producer's test file):
1. No signed requirement for an epic: `blackboard.py claim T-1 --agent worker-a` on epic e-free succeeded with zero flags (exit 0) -- unchanged behaviour confirmed by hand.
2. Signed requirement (dispatch_token.py draft --required + ssh-keygen -Y sign) for epic e-req: `claim T-2 --agent worker-b` with no token refused ("dispatch token required for epic 'e-req' ..."); with the token minted for worker-b but presented as --agent worker-mallory, refused with IDENTITY MISMATCH; with the correct agent it claimed, and the SAME token presented again after resetting the task to review was refused "already used" (single-use at the claim call site, confirmed). `lock.py acquire --token-file` mirrored: refuses with no token under requirement, accepts+refreshes the SAME token twice in a row (non-single-use, by design, for the heartbeat refresh path), refuses a mismatched --holder.
3. Mutation testing in throwaway copies (own mutants, built fresh, not the producer's):
   a. Flipped the IDENTITY MISMATCH comparison (`claimed != actual` -> `claimed == actual`): 6 tests fail, including Falsifiers::test_a_valid_token_is_accepted and test_a_token_for_worker_a_presented_as_worker_b_is_refused. Match check is covered.
   b. Extra mutant named by the dispatch (trust a key named inside the file being checked): patched `_verify_file_signature` to source `allowed_signers` AND the trusted fingerprint from a `trusted_signer_pubkey`/`trusted_signer_fingerprint` field inside the payload itself rather than always `trust/root.pub`. Caught cleanly: baseline passes, mutant fails exactly `Falsifiers::test_a_payload_that_names_its_own_signer_as_trusted_is_still_refused` (a pre-existing T-447 regression test, unrelated to this task's new code, but it is the correct backstop and I independently reproduced the attack and the catch).
   c. GAP FOUND (reported, not blocking): narrowed the identity-match tuple to agent-only (dropped task_id/role) -- `claimed = (claim_agent,)`; `actual = (canonical["agent_name"],)`. This mutant passes the ENTIRE suite (test_dispatch_token.py + test_dispatch_token_wiring.py), because no test anywhere presents a token with the correct agent+task but the wrong role, or correct agent+role but the wrong task -- every existing negative test varies agent_name only. I confirmed by reading the shipped code (not just running it) that the real comparison is the full 3-tuple (dispatch_token.py line ~401), so today's behavior is correct and satisfies acceptance criterion 1 ("a mismatch between token and the acting agent, task or role is refused"); this is a test-coverage gap, not a code defect, but a future edit that silently narrows the tuple would ship undetected. Recommend a follow-up test (same-agent/task, wrong role; same-agent/role, wrong task) before this mechanism is ever required:true on a live epic.

epic_requires_token() calling verify_token_set() rather than verify() (so it does not run T-456's revocation check): read the code, confirmed this is correct by design -- the required flag is an epic-wide property of the signed set, not a per-agent credential, so there is no agent_name to check a revocation against at that point; revocation is still enforced on every individual presented token via verify().

Live tree untouched by my own testing: all mutants and scratch trees built under the session scratchpad, never under the working tree; `git status --porcelain` only shows the producer's own pre-existing diff plus my own blackboard.py-mediated claim/update calls on T-454/T-455.

Verdict: ACCEPT. Both acceptance criteria met, no-flag-day property held under replay, identity mismatch enforced (code-level), single-use/non-single-use nonce split correct. Recorded weakness: no regression test isolates a role-only or task-only mismatch from an agent-only mismatch (c above) -- worth a quick follow-up test before any live epic sets required:true.
